interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is reported absent. Positive surgical margins is reported absent. Seminal vesicle invasion is reported absent. Lymphovascular invasion is documented. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 39.17 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 31.33–47.00 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text: The postoperative pathology reveals a Gleason 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3) and pathological T2 stage with negative surgical margins. A concerning finding is the presence of lymph node metastasis, as documented by the surgical pathology report stating, "lymph node metastasis was present." The seminal vesicles were not invaded, and lymphovascular invasion was present. This adverse finding contrasts with the negative surgical margins. Nodal status is documented as positive metastasis. Preoperative PSA is not recorded, and postoperative PSA is unknown, which prevents assessment of biochemical recurrence. Missing nodal sampling is not applicable as nodal status was documented. The documented presence of lymph node metastasis is a significant adverse factor. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory is crucial for revising the prognosis.

attempts.text: The postoperative pathology revealed a Gleason 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3) and pathological stage pT2. The surgical findings indicated "surgical margins were negative; the seminal vesicles were not invaded; lymphovascular invasion was present; lymph node metastasis was present." The presence of lymph node metastasis is an adverse finding. Countervailing factors include negative surgical margins and non-invasion of the seminal vesicles. Missing postoperative PSA means biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. The status of nodal sampling is documented, which is important for staging. The biopsy-to-prostatectomy differences are not explicitly detailed beyond the surgical pathology report. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are necessary to revise the prognosis.
